title: Forgery of record entries or record instruments
summary: Making, forging, or altering a record-book entry or an instrument purporting to be a record or return specified in section 470, with intent to defraud another.
penalty: Felony alternative: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. Section 473(b) requires misdemeanor treatment for forgery involving a listed check, bond, bank bill, note, cashier’s check, traveler’s check, or money order valued at $950 or less, subject to its specified prior-conviction exceptions. That reduction does not apply when the person is convicted of both forgery and identity theft under section 530.5. Instrument type and value must be checked; the rule is not a blanket reduction of every forgery. These are adult base penalties, not a total sentence prediction. Restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.

title: Wrongful diversion of construction funds
summary: Receiving money for construction services, labor, materials, or equipment, willfully failing to complete the funded improvement or pay for the covered work or items, and wrongfully diverting the funds to another use. A payment dispute or incomplete project alone does not establish these elements.
penalty: If the amount diverted exceeds $2,350: Felony alternative: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. That branch permits a fine up to $10,000, or both the fine and imprisonment. At $2,350 or less the statute declares a misdemeanor; section 19 supplies up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. The threshold is $2,350, not the ordinary theft threshold of $950. These are adult base penalties, not a total sentence prediction. Restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.

penalty: The statute makes the offense grand theft when the specified six-month aggregate exceeds $950; ordinary grand-theft punishment under section 489(c) is Felony alternative: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. title: Theft by keeping lost property without reasonable efforts to return it
summary: Appropriating lost property for oneself or another not entitled to it, when circumstances provide knowledge of or a means to identify the owner, without first making reasonable and just efforts to find the owner and restore the property.
penalty: Ordinary petty theft: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both under section 490.
